Staging (test builds): vault release log

Staging release 33 (test build)

Release 33 lets you choose how agents may use each secret, checks votes more closely, clears more data from memory, and opens release 32 vaults as they are.

Status

Status
Active
Published
2026-11-23
End date
Not set

The current release. New vaults are enrolled into it, and the app offers it to everyone on an older release.

Changes

  • Release 33 opens a vault made by release 32 as it is: nothing is erased and nothing needs to be set up again.
  • Agents: for each secret item an agent can reach, you now choose the ways it may use it: use it inside your vault as before, see the value, run a program with it, or send it to a web API. Every item starts with the first way only. Nothing else is allowed until you turn it on.
  • An agent can now see a secret's value only if you turned that on for the item, and your vault asks you every time. Before, an agent could read any item its rules included without asking you, within their limits. An agent asking for a way you did not turn on is refused.
  • To run a program with a secret, you can list the programs allowed and any other settings an agent may pass to each. With no list, any program may run, and your vault asks you every time. With a list, it asks each time unless you turn that off.
  • Even then, your vault asks when a program is new or has changed, or is a shell, an interpreter or a program that starts other programs. When you approve a program, your vault remembers its exact file and asks again if the file changes.
  • You can also give a run folders of yours to work in, read files from and, if you allow it, write files to. Your vault refuses a run that asks for a folder or file outside them, and always asks you before a run that uses them.
  • Anything that allows an agent more, such as a way, a program, a folder, writing to a folder or a web host, needs your credential's unlock window to be open. Taking something away does not.
  • To send a secret to a web API, you list the hosts allowed. Your vault always asks you first and tells your app the host and header it will be sent with. The value is handed out for at most an hour (15 minutes by default), never past the agent's session.
  • If an agent sends the same request for a secret's value again, your vault now answers only that it was handled. Before, it kept a copy of its answer, value included, for a day, so the agent could get the value this way even after its session ended or it was suspended.
  • To get the value again, the agent must make a new request, which your vault checks and asks you about as usual.
  • Your VettID apps don't show these choices and approvals yet. Until they do, you can't turn these ways on, so an agent can only use a secret inside your vault, and an agent that read secret values before is now refused.
  • Votes: your vault now checks more of what a voting service sends. It checks the rule for how a vote is decided and the outcome the service reports, and treats a result that contradicts itself or does not add up as a failed check.
  • It also checks that each status answer or refusal from the service names your vote, your connection and the time VettID's relay got your request, and keeps as evidence any signed answer showing the service contradicting itself, such as recording a ballot that is not yours.
  • A vote stored by release 32 lacks the decision rule that votes now carry, so after this update its text, choices and count can't be shown and it can't be acted on. Your vault keeps its record. No staging vault holds such a vote: none has been started since release 30.
  • Your vault now clears more copies of decrypted data from memory, and sooner: messages it has read, what it sends, and the handshake with a new device or connection. A vault that is being erased now cuts off its connection to VettID's relay before it destroys its keys.
  • The vault is now built with Go 1.26.11, which fixes a flaw in the Go language's web code (GO-2026-6859). The vault's only web server answers the host's own health check and nothing else on the network, and does not use the affected part, so this changes nothing you would notice.
  • Time scale: 1 day = 1 hour (staging)
  • Built from vettid-vault commit 41de730 (tag release/staging/33) and independently rebuilt on 2026-11-23 with a matching PCR0.

Security

Security fix: update recommended

Release 33 stops your vault keeping a copy of a secret value it gave an agent: before, the same agent could get that value again for up to a day by repeating its request, even after its session ended or it was suspended, and the value stayed in your vault's data after the item was deleted. It also erases a vault in a safer order: before, a vault being erased could wipe its relay key while a request was still signing with it. It clears more copies of decrypted data from memory, and votes check more of what a voting service sends. The Go language's web code had a flaw that could crash some web servers (GO-2026-6859); your vault's only web server does not use the affected part. We know of no use of any of these against any vault. Your PIN and credential password were not exposed. Vaults on releases 30 to 32 are affected.
